label: rem:information-theoretic-time-julia-microscopic
title: Julia-set iteration as the microscopic theory of time
html:
We ground the information-theoretic time (information-theoretic time) in a microscopic dynamical theory: the Julia-set iteration f_q. The thermodynamic limit of this iteration yields the continuous Reeb flow.

Julia set dynamics as the microscopic theory. We interpret the iteration f_q(z) = z^2 + c(q) on the exceptional divisor as the microscopic dynamics of time. Each iterate f_q^{\circ n}(z_0) constitutes one microstate of the temporal evolution. The continuous Reeb flow \phi_t^q emerges as the macroscopic limit, obtained by averaging over t_P(q) microscopic iterates per unit.

The Julia set J(f_q) is the boundary separating escaping and bounded orbits. Its Hausdorff dimension d_H(q) measures the complexity of the time evolution at parameter q. A higher d_H indicates that the microscopic dynamics explores more phase space per operation, so macroscopic time carries more information per unit.
